messages.author: 3e772845e278da9b
messages.subject: passing an object to shiny.
parts:
Hi,

I really like this shiny stuff.  Nice job!  My question comes up about something that I want to do

I have a situation where I have an S4 object that is rich and full of information.  What I want to do is to write a method for that object that will call a shiny script to display the contents of that object.  So for example lets say my object is called "foo" and that it is of class "bar".  I want to be able to write a method that displays bar objects and will launch a shiny app based on foo when I call my display method like this:

display(foo)

## runApp() launches and the user can now get a rich interactive visual of the the contents of "foo".  Sort of like a show() method: but now on steroids...  ;)

Now everything I have described seems straightforward to do except for one thing: How do I pass the object "foo" to my shiny app (without actually serializing it and writng it out to the file system)?  All the inputs for a shiny app seem to be contained in the ui for the app.  That is, I don't seem to be able to pass along anything from my R session.


  Marc

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: passing an object to shiny.
parts:
Just put it in a "global" variable--this can either be in the global environment, or, if you're writing a package, in a package-scoped environment.

If you go the global environment route and don't want the variable to show up for the user, you can name the variable with a leading "." and it won't show up to ls(). And your wrapper function can also rm() the variable when the Shiny app is done executing.
